habitat: Singly or in small groups on coastal lagoons and estuaries or on inland waters. It feeds by probing in the shallows.
summary: A common summer visitor. The underparts are clear white, the bill is straight, slender and black, and the legs are yellow-green. The description also says yellowish legs. The upperparts are sandy-brown with white feather edges, and the back and rump are white in flight. When flushed it calls a soft rapid tjuu-tjuu-tjuu. Newman does not name the months. The Kemp name Marsh Sandpiper and the code NB were left unchanged.

similar.note: Common Greenshank is larger, with a more robust, slightly upturned bill and green-grey legs.

upperparts.pattern: Sandy-brown above, with white feather edges. The identification line includes a white back. In flight the back and rump are white and the feet protrude further than on Greenshank.

underparts.pattern: Clear white underparts. The description says yellowish legs; the identification line says long yellow-green legs.

viewNotes.note: Sandy-brown above, white below, a slender black bill and long yellow-green legs.

calls.description: When put to flight it calls a soft rapid 'tjuu-tjuu-tjuu'. No grade A or grade B recording from South Africa was found. The selected file is a grade A call from Kazakhstan. The filename is XC154257-Tringa stagnatilis calls Zhanteke lake Aqmola province 4 May 2013 (Arend Wassink).mp3.

research.note: Newman calls it a common summer visitor and does not name the months, so status is summer-migrant and monthsPresent is unset. The legs are yellow-green on the identification line and yellowish in the description. Sandy-brown is not a vocabulary colour. No grade A or grade B recording from South Africa was found. The iNaturalist account has no display name, so the login maritzasouthafrica is credited. The Kemp code NB was left unchanged.

population.notes: Kemp et al. 2001 order-of-magnitude threshold 2^10=1024 mature individuals (non-breeding visitor); paper interval half–double → 512–2048.
